subject: B
topic: Sectional revision — GK & Current Affairs India

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and which invading power?
questions.explanation: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali, the Afghan Durrani ruler, who defeated them. Nadir Shah had invaded India earlier in 1739 and sacked Delhi. Babur fought the First Battle of Panipat in 1526. Muhammad Ghori fought at Tarain in the 12th century, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about socio-religious reform movements in India:

(i) The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
(ii) The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda.
(iii) The Aligarh Movement was led by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
(iv) The Theosophical Society in India was founded by Dayananda Saraswati.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj, Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission, and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan led the Aligarh Movement — so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is false because the Theosophical Society was founded by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott, not Dayananda Saraswati; hence options with (iv) are wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:

(i) It is a permanent house that is not subject to dissolution.
(ii) One-third of its members retire every second year.
(iii) The Vice-President of India is its ex-officio Chairman.
(iv) Its members are directly elected by the people.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is permanent, one-third of members retire every two years, and the Vice-President chairs it — so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is false because members are elected indirectly by the elected members of state legislative assemblies, not directly by the people; hence options with (iv) are wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Doctrine of Lapse, used to annex Indian princely states, was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, annexing states like Satara and Jhansi. Lord Cornwallis is known for the Permanent Settlement. Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance. Lord Ripon is remembered for local self-government reforms, so none of them introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian rivers:

(i) The Narmada drains into the Arabian Sea.
(ii) The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India.
(iii) The Krishna rises in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar.
(iv) The Kaveri finally drains into the Arabian Sea.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea, the Godavari is peninsular India's longest river, and the Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar — so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is false because the Kaveri flows east and drains into the Bay of Bengal, not the Arabian Sea; hence options with (iv) are wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states.
Reason (R): The Tropic of Cancer is an imaginary line at about 23.5 degrees north latitude.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Tropic of Cancer crosses eight Indian states, and it lies at about 23.5 degrees north. However, its latitude value does not explain why it passes through exactly eight states, which depends on India's shape and location, so R does not explain A (second option). The other options wrongly deny a true statement or claim a false causal link.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Servants of India Society was founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Reason (R): Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a prominent moderate leader of the Indian National Congress.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: A is false because the Servants of India Society was founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, not Tilak. R is true, as Gokhale was indeed a leading moderate in the Congress. So the fourth option is correct. The first and second wrongly treat A as correct, and the third wrongly calls R incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The classical dance form 'Kuchipudi' originated in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi originated in Andhra Pradesh and takes its name from a village there. Tamil Nadu is home to Bharatanatyam. Kerala is associated with Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Odisha is the birthplace of Odissi, so those states are linked to other dance forms and are incorrect for Kuchipudi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of medals won by a country at four consecutive Games:

2010 → 38
2014 → 64
2018 → 66
2022 → 61

In which year did the country show the highest percentage increase over the previous Games listed?
questions.explanation: The increases are 2014 = 26/38 ≈ 68%, 2018 = 2/64 ≈ 3%, while 2022 shows a decrease. The highest percentage increase is in 2014. '2018' rose only slightly, '2022' actually fell, and they were not equal, so the option claiming they were equal is also incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Viceroy of India passed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, aimed at controlling the Indian-language press?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton enacted the Vernacular Press Act of 1878 to muzzle the Indian-language newspapers. Lord Mayo was assassinated earlier and is linked to financial decentralisation. Lord Curzon is known for the Partition of Bengal. Lord Minto is associated with the Morley-Minto reforms, so those Viceroys are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with their places of origin:

Column I:
(a) Narmada
(b) Godavari
(c) Kaveri
(d) Mahanadi

Column II:
(i) Talakaveri
(ii) Amarkantak
(iii) Sihawa hills (Chhattisgarh)
(iv) Trimbak (Nashik)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Narmada rises at Amarkantak, the Godavari at Trimbak near Nashik, the Kaveri at Talakaveri, and the Mahanadi in the Sihawa hills — matching the first option. The second wrongly swaps Narmada and Godavari. The third wrongly swaps Kaveri and Mahanadi. The fourth wrongly pairs Godavari with Talakaveri, so those are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following countries with their currencies:

Column I:
(a) Japan
(b) Russia
(c) Thailand
(d) South Africa

Column II:
(i) Ruble
(ii) Rand
(iii) Yen
(iv) Baht

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Japan uses the Yen, Russia the Ruble, Thailand the Baht, and South Africa the Rand — matching the first option. The second wrongly swaps Thailand and Russia. The third wrongly swaps Japan and Russia. The fourth wrongly swaps Thailand and South Africa, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are landlocked countries?

(i) Nepal
(ii) Bhutan
(iii) Bangladesh
(iv) Afghanistan

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Nepal, Bhutan and Afghanistan are all landlocked, having no direct access to the sea, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Bangladesh (iii) has a long coastline on the Bay of Bengal and is not landlocked; therefore any option containing (iii) — the second, third and fourth — is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Peace Prize, unlike the other Nobel Prizes, is awarded in which city?
questions.explanation: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway, while the other Nobel Prizes are presented in Stockholm, Sweden. Geneva is a hub of international organisations but not a Nobel venue. Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark and is unrelated to the Nobel ceremonies, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are UNESCO World Heritage Sites located in India?

(i) Group of Monuments at Hampi
(ii) Khajuraho Group of Monuments
(iii) Qutub Minar
(iv) India Gate

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Hampi, Khajuraho and the Qutub Minar are all UNESCO World Heritage Sites, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. India Gate (iv) is a war memorial in Delhi but is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site; hence any option containing (iv) — the second, third and fourth — is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the smallest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Goa is the smallest Indian state by area. Sikkim is the second smallest but larger than Goa. Tripura and Nagaland are small north-eastern states but both larger than Goa in area, so those options are incorrect for the smallest state.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Konark Sun Temple is designed in the shape of a colossal chariot.
Reason (R): The Konark Sun Temple is located in the state of Odisha.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Konark temple is built like a giant chariot with wheels and horses, and it stands in Odisha. But its location does not explain its chariot design, which represents the Sun God's chariot, so R does not explain A (second option). The other options wrongly deny a true statement or claim a false causal link.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The first session of the Indian National Congress, held in 1885, was presided over by __________. __________
questions.explanation: W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first Congress session in Bombay in 1885. Dadabhai Naoroji presided over later sessions, not the first. A. O. Hume was the organising secretary and founder-figure but not the president. Surendranath Banerjee led the Indian Association separately, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first Indian to be appointed as the Deputy Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was independent India's first Deputy Prime Minister, also holding the Home portfolio. Morarji Desai and Charan Singh served as Deputy Prime Minister in later years. Jagjivan Ram also held the post afterwards, but none of them was the first, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's physical geography:

(i) The Deccan Plateau is flanked by the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats.
(ii) K2 is the highest mountain peak lying entirely within Indian territory.
(iii) The Thar Desert lies mainly in the state of Rajasthan.
(iv) The Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and the Brahmaputra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau is bounded by the two Ghats, the Thar Desert lies mainly in Rajasthan, and the Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra — so (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (ii) is false because K2 lies in the Karakoram in Pakistan-administered territory; the highest peak fully within India is Kangchenjunga, so options with (ii) are wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following monuments with the cities where they are located:

Column I:
(a) Charminar
(b) Gateway of India
(c) Hawa Mahal
(d) Victoria Memorial

Column II:
(i) Mumbai
(ii) Jaipur
(iii) Kolkata
(iv) Hyderabad

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Charminar is in Hyderabad, the Gateway of India in Mumbai, the Hawa Mahal in Jaipur, and the Victoria Memorial in Kolkata — matching the first option. The second wrongly swaps Charminar and Gateway of India. The third wrongly swaps Hawa Mahal and Victoria Memorial. The fourth wrongly places Charminar in Jaipur, so those are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Statue of Unity', the world's tallest statue, is dedicated to which national leader?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat honours Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and is the world's tallest statue. It does not depict Mahatma Gandhi, B. R. Ambedkar or Jawaharlal Nehru, each of whom has other memorials but is not the subject of this particular statue, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following authors with their books:

Column I:
(a) R. K. Narayan
(b) Salman Rushdie
(c) Vikram Seth
(d) Chetan Bhagat

Column II:
(i) Midnight's Children
(ii) Malgudi Days
(iii) Five Point Someone
(iv) A Suitable Boy

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: R. K. Narayan wrote Malgudi Days, Salman Rushdie wrote Midnight's Children, Vikram Seth wrote A Suitable Boy, and Chetan Bhagat wrote Five Point Someone — matching the first option. The second swaps Narayan and Rushdie, the third swaps Seth and Bhagat, and the fourth wrongly credits A Suitable Boy to Narayan, so those are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In the Indian Parliament, a Money Bill can be introduced only in which house?
questions.explanation: Under Article 110, a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, on the recommendation of the President. It cannot originate in the Rajya Sabha, which can only suggest changes. 'Either house' is wrong for Money Bills, and a joint sitting is not the place of introduction, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows a country's foodgrain production (in million tonnes):

2019 → 285
2020 → 297
2021 → 310
2022 → 315

What was the total foodgrain production over these four years (in million tonnes)?
questions.explanation: Adding the four figures: 285 + 297 + 310 + 315 = 1207 million tonnes. '1200' and '1210' are close but do not match the exact sum. '1197' understates the total by 10, so those options are incorrect for the combined production.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Poona Sarvajanik Sabha' and later reform work are linked with which early nationalist, often called a pioneer of economic nationalism?
questions.explanation: Mahadev Govind Ranade was a founder of the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha and a pioneer of economic and social reform. Dadabhai Naoroji is known for the 'drain of wealth' theory. Feroze Shah Mehta was a Bombay moderate leader. Surendranath Banerjee founded the Indian Association in Bengal, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the sources of the Indian Constitution:

(i) The idea of the Preamble was drawn from the Constitution of the USA.
(ii) Fundamental Rights were inspired by the Constitution of the USA.
(iii) The parliamentary form of government was adopted from Britain.
(iv) The Directive Principles were borrowed from the Constitution of Canada.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Preamble idea and Fundamental Rights were inspired by the USA, and the parliamentary system came from Britain — so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is false because the Directive Principles were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, not Canada; hence any option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Kanha' and 'Bandhavgarh' national parks, famous for tigers, are located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kanha and Bandhavgarh tiger reserves are both in Madhya Pradesh, often called the 'Tiger State'. Rajasthan has Ranthambore and Sariska, not these parks. Assam is known for Kaziranga and its rhinos. Karnataka has Bandipur and Nagarhole, so those states do not host Kanha and Bandhavgarh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which gas, released in the Bhopal Gas Tragedy of 1984, caused widespread casualties?
questions.explanation: The Bhopal Gas Tragedy was caused by the leak of methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas from a pesticide plant. Carbon monoxide is a common combustion gas but was not the cause here. Sulphur dioxide and chlorine are toxic gases but were not the primary gas released in Bhopal, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India adopted a mixed economy model after independence.
Reason (R): In a mixed economy, both the public sector and the private sector operate together.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A: India is called a mixed economy precisely because both public and private sectors coexist, which is the defining feature R describes. So the first option is correct. The second is wrong because R does explain A. The third and fourth wrongly deny one of the accurate statements.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The famous 'Hornbill Festival', celebrating tribal heritage, is held annually in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland, showcasing the culture of its various tribes. Manipur is known for festivals like Yaoshang. Mizoram celebrates Chapchar Kut. Meghalaya has festivals like Wangala, so those states are associated with different festivals and are incorrect for the Hornbill Festival.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The international agreement adopted in 2015 to limit global warming is known as the __________ Agreement. __________
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement of 2015 committed nations to limiting the rise in global temperatures. The Kyoto Protocol was an earlier 1997 climate treaty. The Montreal Protocol dealt with ozone-depleting substances, not warming. The Geneva Convention concerns humanitarian law, not climate, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are specialised agencies of the United Nations?

(i) UNESCO
(ii) ILO
(iii) Interpol
(iv) FAO

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: UNESCO, the ILO and the FAO are all specialised agencies of the UN, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Interpol (iii) is the International Criminal Police Organization, an independent body not part of the UN system; hence any option containing (iii) — the second, third and fourth — is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Simon Commission' was boycotted by Indians mainly because ______.
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission was boycotted because it was an all-British body with no Indian members, prompting 'Simon Go Back' protests. It did not recommend partition, which came much later. It did not abolish the Congress. It did not deal with the salt tax, which the Dandi March opposed, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the literacy rate (in percent) of a state over four census years:

1991 → 52
2001 → 64
2011 → 74
2021 → 80

Between which two consecutive census years was the increase in percentage points the greatest?
questions.explanation: The point increases were 12 (1991-2001), 10 (2001-2011) and 6 (2011-2021). The greatest rise in percentage points was between 1991 and 2001. '2001 to 2011' rose 10 points and '2011 to 2021' only 6, and the increases were not equal, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Homi Bhabha is regarded as the father of India's nuclear programme.
Reason (R): Homi Bhabha founded the Indian Space Research Organisation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: A is correct: Homi Bhabha is called the father of India's nuclear programme and set up the Atomic Energy Establishment. But R is false because he founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, not ISRO, which grew from Vikram Sarabhai's efforts. So the third option is right. The first and second wrongly treat R as correct, and the fourth wrongly calls A incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Kaziranga National Park', a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is famous for which animal?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga in Assam is renowned for the great one-horned rhinoceros. The Asiatic lion is found in Gir, Gujarat. The snow leopard inhabits the high Himalayas. The Great Indian bustard is protected mainly in Rajasthan's deserts, so those animals are not the highlight of Kaziranga and are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the ASEAN grouping:

(i) It was founded through the Bangkok Declaration.
(ii) Its secretariat is located in Jakarta.
(iii) India is a full member of ASEAN.
(iv) It promotes economic cooperation among Southeast Asian nations.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded by the Bangkok Declaration, has its secretariat in Jakarta, and promotes regional economic cooperation — so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (iii) is false because India is a dialogue partner, not a full member of ASEAN; hence any option containing (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Golden Revolution' in India is associated with the growth of which sector?
questions.explanation: The Golden Revolution refers to the boom in horticulture, fruits and honey production. The White Revolution relates to milk (Operation Flood). The Green Revolution concerns foodgrains like wheat and rice. The Blue Revolution deals with fisheries, so those options describe different revolutions and are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following sports personalities with their sports:

Column I:
(a) Viswanathan Anand
(b) Pankaj Advani
(c) Pullela Gopichand
(d) Dhanraj Pillay

Column II:
(i) Badminton
(ii) Field hockey
(iii) Chess
(iv) Billiards and snooker

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Viswanathan Anand plays chess, Pankaj Advani excels at billiards and snooker, Pullela Gopichand is a badminton figure, and Dhanraj Pillay was a hockey player — matching the first option. The second swaps Advani and Gopichand, the third swaps Anand and Advani, and the fourth swaps Gopichand and Pillay, so those are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Preamble' to the Indian Constitution begins with which words?
options: In the name of the people
questions.explanation: The Preamble opens with 'We, the people of India', showing that the Constitution derives its authority from the people. 'India, that is Bharat' is the opening of Article 1, not the Preamble. 'We, the citizens of India' and 'In the name of the people' are incorrect phrasings not used at the start, so those options are wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which committee recommended the establishment of Panchayati Raj institutions in India in 1957?
questions.explanation: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system. The Ashok Mehta Committee later suggested a two-tier structure. The Sarkaria Commission dealt with Centre-State relations. The Kothari Commission focused on education, so those bodies are incorrect for the 1957 recommendation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: A scheme was launched in a certain year, and its 25th anniversary was celebrated in 2020. In which year was the scheme launched?
questions.explanation: A 25th anniversary in 2020 means the scheme began 25 years earlier, that is 2020 − 25 = 1995. '1990' would give a 30th anniversary in 2020. '2000' would give only a 20th anniversary. '1985' would mark a 35th anniversary, so those years are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following awards are given in the field of cinema?

(i) Dadasaheb Phalke Award
(ii) National Film Award
(iii) Filmfare Award
(iv) Dronacharya Award

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the National Film Award and the Filmfare Award are all cinema honours, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. The Dronacharya Award (iv) is given to sports coaches, not for cinema; hence any option containing (iv) — the second, third and fourth — is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign trade:

(i) A trade deficit occurs when imports exceed exports.
(ii) Petroleum is one of India's major imports.
(iii) The balance of trade includes only visible items (goods).
(iv) The Directorate General of Foreign Trade functions under the Ministry of Commerce.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct: a trade deficit means imports exceed exports, petroleum is a major import, the balance of trade covers only visible goods (services are in the balance of payments), and the DGFT works under the Ministry of Commerce. Since every statement is accurate, options limited to three are incomplete and incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Jallikattu', a traditional bull-taming sport, is associated with which state's harvest festival?
questions.explanation: Jallikattu is a bull-taming event held during the Pongal harvest festival in Tamil Nadu. Kerala celebrates Onam with different customs. Karnataka has its own festivals like Kambala buffalo racing. Andhra Pradesh observes Sankranti but is not linked to Jallikattu, so those states are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs of dance forms and their states are correctly matched?

(i) Bihu — Assam
(ii) Garba — Gujarat
(iii) Bhangra — Punjab
(iv) Yakshagana — West Bengal

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Bihu belongs to Assam, Garba to Gujarat and Bhangra to Punjab, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correctly matched. Pair (iv) is wrong because Yakshagana is a folk theatre of Karnataka, not West Bengal; hence any option containing (iv) — the second, third and fourth — is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about international boundary lines:

(i) The McMahon Line separates India and China in the eastern sector.
(ii) The Durand Line lies between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
(iii) The 38th Parallel divides North Korea and South Korea.
(iv) The Radcliffe Line separates India and Nepal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line is the India-China boundary in the east, the Durand Line lies between Pakistan and Afghanistan, and the 38th Parallel divides the two Koreas — so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is false because the Radcliffe Line separates India and Pakistan, not India and Nepal; hence options with (iv) are wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Morley-Minto Reforms' of 1909 are best known for introducing which feature into Indian governance?
questions.explanation: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Provincial autonomy came with the Government of India Act, 1935. Adult franchise was adopted after independence. A federal court was also set up under the 1935 Act, not in 1909, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In an election to the 543-seat Lok Sabha, a party won 303 seats. By how many seats did it exceed the halfway majority mark of 272 seats?
questions.explanation: The party's margin over the majority mark is 303 − 272 = 31 seats. '29' and '30' understate the difference. '33' overstates it. Only 31 correctly represents how far 303 exceeds the 272-seat majority threshold, so the other options are incorrect.
